title: git-cicd verdict is present and pending from the moment the workflow starts
body:
Unit 3 of plan `mdci-dev-6692` (record: `.pearls/docs/epics/mdci-dev-6692.md` in `mangimangi/medici-dev`). Decided with the owner on 2026-11-27: "I agree we should fix...I think pending w status write is ok".

## What happens today

The interface git-cicd was built to says: "One always-present check with a fixed name ... so anything waiting on 'checks pass' is never left hanging", and that "nothing ran" is never read as "passed". In v0.0.1 the check `git-cicd verdict` is the **last** thing to appear on a pull request. The generated workflow (`templates/workflow.yml`) is `decide`, then one runner per needed job, then `verdict`; GitHub creates a check run for a job only when that job is queued, and `verdict` is queued after the others finish. Between `decide` finishing and the job runners being queued, every check that exists on the commit is green.

That window was hit on the first repository to adopt git-cicd. On medici #177 (2026-11-27), medici's walker waited for the pull request's checks, saw "1 reported, none failed or pending" (the vendor-file check), and merged at about 16:15:40 UTC. `git-cicd decide` finished at 16:15:46; `unit-tests` and `toolchain-contract` started at 16:15:48; `git-cicd verdict` finished green at 16:20:24, four and a half minutes after the merge. Any reader that merges when no check is failing or pending can do the same on any repository that uses git-cicd.

The same window exists when no job is needed, and when `decide` itself has not started yet.

## Required behaviour

From the moment the git-cicd workflow starts on a pull request, something named `git-cicd verdict` is on the pull request's head commit and is **pending**, and it stays pending until the verdict is known. It then becomes success or failure exactly as the verdict is today (failed when a blocking job failed or could not run, or when the workflow does not match the config; otherwise passed, including when no job was needed). At no moment after the workflow has started is every check on the commit green while the verdict is still to come. A workflow run that is cancelled or superseded, or that dies before the verdict, does not leave `git-cicd verdict` green.

The owner accepted the cost: on the `open` moment the workflow's token may write commit statuses, as a narrow exception to "read-only on `open`". It gets that one write permission and no other; contents stay read-only. Nothing else about the interface changes: only the cron block of the generated file varies with the config; `verify` still compares the whole file; every fact about the change still reaches the tool as an environment variable.

A reader must not be shown two things of the same name that disagree: if both a status and a check run carry the name `git-cicd verdict`, they never show one green while the other is pending, and the documentation says which one a reader (a person, branch protection, a script that lists a pull request's checks) should rely on.

If this cannot be had with GitHub Actions as required, stop and say so (`madp stop "<question>"`) with what was found; do not ship something that narrows the window without closing it.

## Acceptance criteria

- On this issue's own pull request into `plan/mdci-dev-6692`, `git-cicd verdict` is pending on the head commit before git-cicd's `test` job has finished, and ends green; the pull request description gives the evidence (timestamps of the pending state and of the `test` job, read from the platform, not asserted).
- With no job needed (a change only to files in `needs_nothing`), `git-cicd verdict` is pending from the start of the run and ends green with the "0 of N jobs needed" text.
- When a blocking job fails, `git-cicd verdict` ends failed.
- The generated workflow grants, on the pull request trigger, the status-write permission and no other write permission; a test asserts the permissions block.
- Two configs that differ only in jobs that are not `cron` still generate the same file, and `verify` still fails on a hand edit.
- `README.md` says the verdict is present and pending from the start, names the permission and why, and says which object a reader should wait on.
- The tests pass; `python3 .vendored/check` reports no violation; the checks on this issue's pull request are seen green, including `git-cicd verdict`, before the work is called done.
- git-cicd's own `.github/workflows/git-cicd.yml` is regenerated and committed with the change.

## Out of scope

The `merge` and `cron` moments and manual runs. Any change to git-vendored or git-semver, or to a vendor-protected file. Any change in medici or another consumer: they pick the fix up by installing the release and regenerating their workflow.
